scenes.title: Cold open
narration: Isolations in the Underground: How California Re-Engineered Belly Dance
This is Tribal Fusion Belly Dance. Late 1990s to present.
on_screen: Hero video, first 10 seconds (8XGIRLwcw4o)
Title card: Tribal Fusion Belly Dance · United States · Late 1990s to present

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Tribal Fusion emerged from the California belly dance lineage tracing back to Jamila Salimpour, who founded the troupe Bal Anat in the late 1960s to present theatrical Middle Eastern and North African styles at California Renaissance fairs.
Jamila taught Masha Archer of the San Francisco Classic Dance Troupe, who in turn taught Carolena Nericcio, the founder of FatChanceBellyDance and pioneer of American Tribal Style (ATS).
on_screen: Map: United States · North America
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Tribal Fusion is primarily a theatrical and performance art form rather than a social or ritual dance.
It is performed on concert stages, community haflas, circus-theatre showcases, and alternative music events.

Moving away from the commercial cabaret nightclub format, it emphasizes artistic self-expression, bodily mastery, strength, and female stage presence uncoupled from exoticized male-gaze entertainment.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Belly Dance: Cues and Tattoos Festival 2015 - Bindu Bolar Tribalina. (https://archive.org/details/cues-and-tattoos-festival-2015-bindu-bolar-tribalina)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Unlike the strictly group-led, cue-based structured improvisation of FatChanceBellyDance, Tribal Fusion is predominantly choreographed and can be performed as a solo, duet, or group piece.
Dancers maintain an upright lifted posture while executing hyper-articulated isolations, including popping contractions, belly rolls, serpentine arm paths, and hip locks.
Dancers integrate technique derived from Suhaila Salimpour, hip hop popping, flamenco arm carriage, and Indian classical forms like Kathak and Odissi.
Watch for Snake Arms, Belly Roll, Ribcage Isolation Slide.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (8XGIRLwcw4o)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Fluid stage floor patterns, direct audience address, diagonal transitions, and stationary solo pedestals.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Tribal Fusion evolved alongside late-1990s and early-2000s electronica, trip-hop, and world fusion.
Producers and DJs merged traditional Middle Eastern acoustic instruments—such as darbuka, riqq, and oud—with synthesized beats, deep bass lines, and breakbeats.
Listen for the Electronic synthesizers, Drum machines and sampled percussion, Darbuka/Doumbek, Riqq.
The pulse is 4/4 at about 80 beats a minute.

A dense synthesis of subterranean sub-bass, digitized breakbeats, and acoustic Middle Eastern percussion, textured with swirling ambient synthesizer pads, melancholic string motifs, and occasional swing or jazz brass accents.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Costuming varies between rich maximalism and sleek modern minimalism.

The adorned aesthetic, popularized by Mardi Love and The Indigo, features layered skirts, Tulle bi telli fabrics, antique tribal jewelry, Afghan guls, Indian shisha mirrors, and Rajasthani cowrie shells braided into the hair with dyed yarn.
Tattoos, body piercings, and dramatic stage makeup are common.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Seminal figures include Jill Parker ('mama of Tribal Fusion'), Heather Stants (founder of Urban Tribal Dance Company), Rachel Brice (foremost soloist and co-founder of The Indigo), Mardi Love (costume innovator and core member of The Indigo), Zoe Jakes (co-founder of Beats Antique), Suhaila Salimpour (whose isolation technique heavily influenced the movement), Ariellah Aflalo (Dark Fusion pioneer), and producer Miles Copeland.

Variants include Urban Tribal, developed in San Diego with modern dance and street aesthetics; Dark Fusion, initiated by Ariellah Aflalo blending gothic elements; Vaudeville or Tribal Vintage, drawing from pre-WWII jazz, swing, and burlesque eras; and Improvisational Tribal Style (ITS), developed by Amy Sigil as an alternate group-improvisation framework.

Traced through a direct teacher-student chain: Jamila Salimpour taught Masha Archer; Archer taught Carolena Nericcio (creator of ATS); Nericcio taught Jill Parker; Parker inspired Heather Stants and Mardi Love; technique was further shaped by Suhaila Salimpour; Rachel Brice consolidated these lines to form Tribal Fusion.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Tribal Fusion Belly Dance is parent of American Tribal Style Belly Dance: Tribal Fusion set its technical and costuming foundation directly from American Tribal Style (ATS).
Tribal Fusion Belly Dance is influence of Egyptian Cabaret Belly Dance: Tribal Fusion incorporates movements, music concepts, and stylistic accents from Egyptian cabaret traditions.
Tribal Fusion Belly Dance is influence of Popping: Dancers integrate muscular contractions, pops, and locks adapted from street dance and popping.
Tribal Fusion Belly Dance is influence of Flamenco: Contributes to the proud lifted upper-body posture, skirt work, and dramatic arm carriage.

scenes.title: Body and posture
narration: Grounded lower body with soft knees, an elevated and wide ribcage, engaged core, flat lower back, and lengthened neck with relaxed shoulders.
Sinuous snake arms undulating through shoulders, elbows, and wrists; stark geometric framing influenced by flamenco and popping; delicate Mudra-inspired hand placement.
Precise separation between thoracic and pelvic compartments; rolling abdominal undulations; sharp popping locks of the pelvis; figure-eight hip pathways.

scenes.title: Step A — slowly
narration: Step 1: Lift ribcage and drop shoulders into an aligned, grounded stance with soft knees.
Step 2: Execute an upper-torso chest slide side-to-side without moving the hips.
Footwork from the sources: Slow deliberate stepping, lunges, and controlled weight transfers coordinated with rhythmic counts; footwork remains subordinate to upper-body and pelvic isolations.
Drill: Stand with feet parallel, soften knees, tuck tailbone, and lift chest.
on_screen: Instructor front view, then back view (student's perspective); three repetitions
Counts on screen

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer
narration: Step 3: Roll the abdomen sequentially in an undulating belly roll, pulling inward from top to bottom.
Step 4: Perform a sharp pelvic tuck and release isolation (lock or pop) on a percussive beat count.
Drill: Perform horizontal chest slides side-to-side on a 4-count rhythm without hip movement.
on_screen: Instructor front and back view; slow, then half tempo

scenes.title: Put it together
narration: Step A, then Step B, without stopping. Slow first.
Now half tempo. Now full tempo.
Mirror: the instructor faces you and mirrors, so your right is your right.
Drill: Practice continuous snake arms moving from shoulder to fingertip for 16 counts.
